stage.smallBody: Open a family member’s app below, or follow the seven scenes. The Demo controls let you switch people.

1.title: Set the boundary
1.cue: On Minh’s phone, tap “Set the limit”: verified payees only, up to the invoice, until March. Sign with the passkey.
1.say: Humans set the goal and the boundary once.

2.title: Linh forwards the invoice
2.cue: Linh starts vague in Vietnamese; the agent asks for the invoice instead of guessing. Then she forwards it and the agent checks the signature, the payee credential, the rules and the quote.
2.say: Payee, amount and destination never come from the AI.

3.title: Minh approves the exact action
3.cue: Minh gets one card: what he pays in VND, what Hanbit receives in KRW, rate and margin, verified payee, paperwork ready. Approve with the passkey; Linh's thread says the money is on its way. Skip the 30-minute cancel window to watch it reach PAID.
3.say: Under a minute, in Vietnamese, on a phone.

4.title: The attack
4.cue: Linh forwards a “15% early payment discount” email with a new account. The red card explains what was attempted and why it was stopped.
4.say: Text in an email can never become a payee.
4.cue2: Then the pressure scam: a “police” message demands a deposit to a “safe account”. Everything pauses for 24 hours and Lan, at home in Đà Nẵng, gets one calm request to check with Linh.

5.title: Visa refused
5.cue: A week later the visa is refused. Linh forwards the letter and signs two forms herself: cancel admission and the refund request. The money can only go back to Minh. A “refund agent” tries to redirect it and is denied. Jump to Hanbit's promise, two weeks after classes start, and Minh sees what came back and why it is a little less.
5.say: Nobody else owns this unhappy path end to end.

6.title: Prove it
6.cue: In the Trust center, change one byte of the log and press Verify: it pinpoints the entry and the anchor. Restore and verify again.

7.title: Routine autonomy
7.cue: Switch to the Wang family (CN→KR, Chinese UI). Hao asks to pay rent; the assistant asks for the rental agreement and a rent limit. Hao uploads the lease (checked against the bank's record), Wang sets the monthly limit for the name-checked landlord, and rent goes out on its own, inside the limit, with a notification and a cancel window.
7.say: The agent participates, inside boundaries humans set.

s1.text: Australian student visa applications refused in FY2025-26. Families pay tuition before they know the outcome.

s2.text: Typical wait for a refusal refund, re-converted at the refund-day rate, often minus fees and retentions.

s3.text: The “early payment discount” fake invoices offer, with a brand-new account. A classic tuition scam.

moments.title: One calm concierge for the family’s biggest transfer of the year

pay.title: Pays only the real university
pay.body: The agent reads the invoice, checks the university’s signed payee credential, gets an all-in quote and builds the bank paperwork. The parent signs exactly that.

attack.title: Stops the fake invoice
attack.body: A discount email with a new account goes nowhere: the account was never vouched for and the details came from untrusted text. The family sees why, in plain words.

refund.title: Brings the money home
refund.body: When the visa is refused, the agent files the claim, chases on schedule and refuses any redirect. The refund can only return to the account that paid.

tiers.title: The AI proposes. The policy engine decides.
tiers.lead: Every action is wrapped in an envelope and judged by deterministic rules outside the model. The model never holds credentials and never supplies a payee, amount or destination.

L0.name: Inform
L0.body: Explain invoices, deadlines, rules and the all-in cost.

L1.name: Prepare
L1.body: Read documents, build the paperwork pack, draft claims. Nothing leaves.

L2.name: Execute within mandate
L2.body: Same checked payee, under the signed cap, no taint, with a cancel window.

L3.name: Step up
L3.body: First payment, new payee, anything risky: the parent signs the exact action.

LX.name: Never
LX.body: Raise its own limit, add payees from text, redirect refunds, split to dodge quotas, crypto.

proof.title: Change one byte and the log tells you where
proof.lead: Each decision is hash-chained to the one before and anchored in Merkle batches on a permissioned FISCO BCOS chain. Only hashes go on chain.
proof.cta: Try it in the Trust center

cosigner.quietBody: You are the family’s second signature. We only ask you when something looks like a scam, never for routine payments.
cosigner.role1: Check by phone that Linh and Minh are safe before any unusual money moves.
cosigner.role2: Confirm when a request is a scam, so the family can close it calmly.
cosigner.role3: Nobody can ask you to send money. Your signature can never pay an unverified account.
cosigner.title: Someone is pressuring the family to send money
cosigner.body: A message posing as the police asked for a “proof-of-funds deposit” into a “safe account” and said to keep it secret. Nothing has been sent.
cosigner.whyTitle: Why it looks like a scam
cosigner.toldTitle: What Linh and Minh were told
cosigner.told1: Nothing was sent. That account can never be paid through BursarBridge.
cosigner.told2: Real police, embassies and universities never ask for deposits or secrecy.
cosigner.told3: Everything stays paused for 24 hours while the family checks.
cosigner.do1: Call Linh yourself, on the number you always use. Never a number from the message.
cosigner.do2: Talk to Minh before anyone sends anything.
cosigner.do3: If you can’t reach Linh, call the police yourself on 113.
cosigner.signHint: Your signature records that you checked with Linh. It can never make that account payable.
cosigner.cantReachBody: Keep trying her usual number and call Minh. Nothing can be sent while this is paused. If you are worried for Linh’s safety, call 113.
cosigner.signedBody: Your check is recorded. Minh can now close the request. The money stays where it is.
